title: Mods in Claude Code: change how Claude Code works
format_note: Presenter intro for 5.7s, then a 115s continuous screen recording of a desktop app that is zoomed and dimmed to follow the narration, then 3s logo card.
one_thing: A mod is just a plugin with one extra key, and it can change what Claude Code renders; hiding emails until hover proves it in one worked example.

transcript.voice_style: Fast, friendly first-person explainer; plain verbs, concrete wants ('I always wanted more visibility'), analogies to Express middleware.
transcript.script_shape: Claim, three one-line examples, how it works (plugin, hook, three arguments), how to load, build one live, share it. Each beat is narrated over the exact code or UI it names.

structure.frame0: Presenter face fills frame, mid-word, warm interior background; subject present, not black or a logo (f0001.jpg). Mean luminance 0.30, contentfulCells 0.2.
structure.first_3s: Presenter says 'We just added mods to Claude Code' and states the promise: change how Claude Code works. Hands move at 0.3-0.7s (strips/window-01-0.1s.jpg). No title card or caption.

beats.what: On-camera presenter announces mods and the promise to change how Claude Code works.

Agents panel: /agents-panel opens a side pane listing seven agents with run buttons (f0016.jpg).
Email mod: customers.csv answer shows the email masked; the hover reveal is said, not shown.
Anatomy: plugin.json, hooks.json 'modules' key, register.tsx opened; camera zooms to the on(...) line.
Walk through the three arguments $, e, next with selection highlights, zoom and dimming of other lines.
Loading: blurred terminal with claude --plugin-dir flag, then settings.json env lines for the desktop app; context bar reloads.
Build the hide-email mod: EMAIL regex, masked and shown styles, ui.render on AssistantMessage.
Ask for Sam's email: masked block; ask for a thank-you: command uses the real address (f0088.jpg, f0091.jpg).
marketplace.json lists three mods (f0097.jpg); /plugin install hide-email@my-mods typed in terminal.
Cut to warm off-white card with Claude Code starburst and wordmark.

good.observation: Frame 0 is the presenter already speaking, so the hook claim lands inside the first 2.1s and no logo card delays it.
The same examples are announced early and then built later. The email mod is shown at 0:32 and rebuilt at 2:16, which makes the explanation feel earned.
Camera zoom plus dimming isolates the exact token the narrator names ($, e, next), one focal point per frame at 3x size.
Proof is shown inside the product: redacted email in the answer, real address in the command that follows.
Real product text is on screen, legible after zoom: the context bar shows exact token counts and percentages.
Quiet restrained end: install command, then a 3.2s cream logo card, with no slogan.

weak.observation: Window-level views carry 8-10px text, so at phone width the chat and sidebar are unreadable until zoomed.
Long static stretches: 63.6% of 2s intervals have no change, with a 28s static run ending at 102s.
The hover reveal, the claimed payoff of the email mod, is never shown on screen; only the masked state is.
Narration runs about 220 words a minute with no visible text support for the terms $send, next and event.

rule_candidates.rule: In a tutorial, hold one frame composition for as long as its narrated line runs and let a zoom or dim change the focus; do not cut. Used here for 116s between cuts.
rule_candidates.evidence: rhythm.longest_shot 116.02s, 57.8% of runtime; 3 hard cuts in 200.6s

rule_candidates.rule: Open a tutorial with the presenter speaking on frame 0 and state the promise within 2.5s; no card, no caption.
Zoom to roughly 3x on the exact token being named and dim the rest to about a quarter contrast so the viewer sees one thing at a time.
rule_candidates.evidence: f0043.jpg, f0049.jpg; code line 27px = 3.75% of height

rule_candidates.rule: Show a claim working inside the product before explaining it, then prove its limit with a second action. Here the masked email is followed by a command using the real one.
Use a presenter-to-screen hard cut at the first demonstrable noun, within 6s of start, and make it the only cut for the first 120s.
Screen-recording text under 12px at 1280 wide fails at phone width; give each such region a zoom of at least 2x before the narration depends on it.
Introduce the on-screen product with a state that has its own motion (a measuring bar, a spinner, a typing prompt) so a static screen still shows change every 2-3s.
End with a quiet logo card held at least 3s after the final action, with no line of copy.
